phase: Phase 2 — classification and architecture mapping only. Nothing here executes; the health engine does not read this file.

archetypes.record_predicate: Per-record field-state or timestamp predicate on one task table
archetypes.aggregate_distribution: Count, ratio, share, distribution, dominance or trend over a slice, judged against a threshold
archetypes.configuration_inspection: Reads platform configuration objects and compares them with usage
archetypes.reference_integrity: A reference field must resolve to an existing, active or valid-state target
archetypes.cross_record_linkage: Existence or state of RELATED records in another ITSM table (incident↔problem↔change↔KB, approvals, tasks)
archetypes.relationship_graph: Needs the CMDB relationship graph: degree, traversal to a service, dependent CIs
archetypes.audit_history: Needs sys_audit, journal or task_sla event history to reconstruct transitions or timing
archetypes.text_analysis: Similarity, clustering, normalised-frequency, semantic consistency or pattern (regex) analysis over free text
archetypes.temporal_correlation: Correlates events across records or tables by CI and time window
archetypes.composite: Derives from other rules’ outputs or needs three or more distinct mechanisms in sequence

conventions.UNDEFINED: The workbook does not state it and nothing was invented. Appears in time_window, fields, configuration_objects and implementation_notes.
conventions.tables: Only tables the workbook names, or that a named field belongs to unambiguously (incident.close_code → incident).
conventions.candidate_tables: Platform tables INFERRED from a workbook concept the sheet does not name (“assignment rule definitions” → sysrule_assignment). Verify on the instance before use.
conventions.tables_undefined: true when the rule needs an object the workbook names only as a concept and no platform table can be stated with confidence (MIM communication plans, PIRs, CAB, conflict results, change calendar).
conventions.existing_engine_support: FULL = a per-record predicate over incident/change_request/problem fields (fields may be added to the extraction spec) with no other table, history, text analysis, configuration or aggregate threshold. PARTIAL = an existing utility is reusable (extraction, in-memory join over already-extracted tables, the relationship graph, sla.js, schema.js, dba-schema, countBy, kpis/measures, cmdb-signals) but at least one new component is needed. NONE = needs a mechanism with no implementation: bulk audit/journal reads, text similarity/clustering/regex scanning, cross-table time-window correlation, inter-rule composition, or a platform object with no reader.
conventions.volume: Data the rule must touch under its recommended strategy. scale_risk marks rules that need row-level retrieval of a large table with no aggregate pushdown, or an audit/text pass — the ones that become a problem at millions of records.
conventions.dependencies: consumes_output_of = cannot be computed without that rule’s result; interpret_with = the workbook says report alongside / conditional on / precondition; related = the workbook’s causal cross-links (root cause of, suppresses, feeds, joins); external = other domains’ rules, baseline data or customer inputs. A dependency never merges two rules.
conventions.threshold_default: Copied verbatim from the catalogue (Threshold / Parameter). Not normalised.

entries.rule: Priority matrix producing a single dominant priority (>70% in one band)
configuration_objects: priority lookup configuration (candidate: dl_u_priority data lookup)
entries.threshold_default: Default 70% in one band. Window default 90 days.
entries.support_reason: priority/impact/urgency are already extracted for incident, so the distribution is computable in memory today; missing: an aggregate evaluator with a dominance threshold, an estate-level finding that carries a metric, and a reader for the priority matrix configuration.
entries.volume_reason: Distribution over every incident in the window. Aggregate API group-by priority (and by group) reduces it to a handful of counts.
entries.implementation_notes: Aggregate API with sysparm_group_by=priority answers the share per band; a second group-by on assignment_group answers "by group". client.countBy supports one group-by field today.

entries.rule: Categorisation taxonomy with categories never used, or one category absorbing most volume
entries.threshold_default: Unused = zero use in 180 days. Dominance threshold default 40%.
entries.support_reason: servicenow/schema.js getSchema() already returns the sys_choice list per field; usage per value is one Aggregate API group-by. Missing: the comparison of configured set vs used set, the dominance threshold (40%) and the subcategory spread evidence.
entries.volume_reason: One group-by over the 180-day incident slice plus the choice list.
entries.implementation_notes: Cross-domain link says this blocks ITSM-054; that is a downstream dependency (054 depends on category quality), not an input to this rule.

entries.rule: No SLA definition attached to a priority band
configuration_objects: SLA definitions (contract_sla) and their start conditions
entries.threshold_default: Any band with non-zero volume and no SLA
entries.support_reason: servicenow/sla.js listSlas()/getSla() read definitions and conditions; incident volume per priority is one group-by. Missing: evaluating which priority bands a start condition covers (condition parsing against the band set).
entries.volume_reason: Tens of SLA definitions and one group-by count.
entries.implementation_notes: Evidence asks for "reported compliance with and without uncovered bands" — that half needs task_sla aggregates (see ITSM-033).

entries.rule: Assignment rules absent, so routing is fully manual
configuration_objects: assignment rule definitions (workbook does not name the table; candidate sysrule_assignment)
entries.threshold_default: Report as a ratio of total volume
entries.support_reason: No reader for assignment rules exists, and "incident volume with no matching rule at creation" needs either rule-condition evaluation per incident or the first-set value of assignment_group from sys_audit. Neither mechanism exists.
entries.volume_reason: Every incident in the window must be tested against every rule condition, or its assignment audit read.
entries.implementation_notes: Evidence (reassignment count distribution, time-to-first-assignment) needs incident.reassignment_count and audit timing.

entries.rule: Impact and urgency fields not driving priority (priority set manually, overriding matrix)
entries.threshold_default: Report as a ratio and by group
entries.support_reason: The comparison priority != matrix(impact, urgency) is a per-record predicate over fields incident already carries (impact/urgency need adding to the spec); the matrix itself must be read from configuration, and "by user / direction" evidence needs sys_audit on the priority field.
entries.volume_reason: Row-level over the slice if done in memory; an Aggregate API group-by (impact, urgency, priority) collapses it to at most 25 combinations.
entries.implementation_notes: Multi-field group-by is not wrapped in client.js yet (countBy takes one field).

entries.rule: Category-subcategory combinations invalid or orphaned
entries.threshold_default: Any invalid pair with non-zero volume
entries.support_reason: Choice lists are readable through schema.js / dba-schema listChoices; the used pairs are one two-field group-by. Missing: dependent_value in the choice read and the set comparison.
entries.volume_reason: One group-by over the slice plus the choice configuration.

entries.rule: Auto-close duration set so short that resolution verification is impossible
configuration_objects: auto-close configuration (workbook does not name it; candidate sys_properties glide.ui.autoclose.time)
entries.threshold_default: Default minimum 3 business days. Compare against the reopen timing distribution.
entries.support_reason: Three mechanisms in sequence: read the auto-close duration (no config reader), build the reopen timing distribution (needs reopen event timing from audit or incident.reopened_time), then correlate reopen clustering against the window. None exists.
entries.volume_reason: Reopen timing for every resolved incident in the window.
entries.implementation_notes: Threshold "3 business days" needs a schedule (cmn_schedule) to convert to business time — UNDEFINED which schedule.

entries.rule: Resolution code list with a dominant catch-all value ("Other", "Resolved")
entries.support_reason: One group-by on close_code plus the choice list from schema.js; missing: dominance evaluator, the definition of "catch-all/generic" values (UNDEFINED which values count), and by-group breakdown.
entries.implementation_notes: Which close codes are "generic" is not defined by the workbook beyond the examples "Other", "Resolved".

entries.rule: State model with unreachable or dead-end states
configuration_objects: state transition configuration (UNDEFINED — the platform keeps incident state transitions in scripts/flows, not one table)
entries.threshold_default: Age threshold default 30 days for dead-end detection
entries.support_reason: States with zero records is a group-by plus the choice list (reusable); "no outbound transition" needs a transition map, and no reader for state transition configuration exists or is clearly derivable.
entries.volume_reason: Group-by state plus per-record age for records in dead-end states.

entries.rule: Mandatory fields enforced at the wrong state (too late to be useful)
configuration_objects: UI policy and data policy mandatory configuration by state (candidates: sys_ui_policy/_action, sys_data_policy2/_rule)
entries.support_reason: No reader for UI/data policies, and "population timing from audit" needs bulk sys_audit per field. The field-to-stage value mapping is itself UNDEFINED (configurable, no default).
entries.volume_reason: Population timing means the audit row of the first write per field per record.

entries.rule: Notification rules firing to inactive users or empty groups
entries.support_reason: No notification-rule reader; recipient resolution (users, groups, event-parm recipients) is bespoke. Membership resolution itself is the same join ITSM-018 needs.
entries.volume_reason: Tens to hundreds of notification rules.
entries.implementation_notes: "Firing volume and incidents affected" evidence needs sys_email/sysevent history — UNDEFINED retention.

entries.rule: Business hours / schedule not applied to SLA calculation
entries.threshold_default: Compare against the service commitment where one exists
entries.support_reason: sla.js already reads definitions, schedules and schedule_source (and documents the inert-schedule trap). Missing: commitment records (UNDEFINED source) and the breach distribution by day-of-week/hour over task_sla.
entries.volume_reason: Definitions are few; breach-by-weekday needs a group-by over task_sla.

entries.rule: Custom incident states added without corresponding SLA handling
configuration_objects: incident state choices vs OOB set (OOB baseline UNDEFINED — must be supplied)
entries.threshold_default: Any custom state absent from SLA conditions
entries.support_reason: Choices via schema.js, SLA conditions via sla.js, volume per state via group-by. Missing: an OOB state baseline to define "custom", and condition parsing to see which states the pause/stop conditions reference.
entries.volume_reason: Choice list and definitions; one group-by.
entries.implementation_notes: "Time spent in it" evidence needs state-duration history (audit).

entries.rule: Incident form with excessive custom fields, unpopulated
configuration_objects: custom fields on incident (sys_dictionary; "custom" criterion UNDEFINED — u_ prefix or non-system creator)
entries.support_reason: dba-schema listFields() reads the dictionary with creator metadata; population rate is one count per field (fieldISNOTEMPTY). Missing: the custom-field criterion, the per-field count loop and the 5% threshold.
entries.volume_reason: One Aggregate API count per custom field (N small) over the slice.

entries.rule: Knowledge suggestion not enabled on incident
configuration_objects: knowledge suggestion configuration on incident (UNDEFINED table; candidate contextual search cxs_table_config)
entries.threshold_default: Fires only where published articles exist
entries.support_reason: No reader for the knowledge-suggestion / contextual-search configuration; kb_knowledge is not in the allow-list.

entries.rule: Percentage of incidents with no CI and no service reference
entries.support_reason: Both fields are in the incident spec and the existing ITSM-INC-NO-CI predicate already tests them per record; the ratio, the 40% threshold, the trend (measures history pattern exists for CMDB-038) and the by-category/group breakdown are missing.
entries.volume_reason: Whole slice; two Aggregate API counts (or group-bys) make it cheap.
entries.implementation_notes: Feeds ITSM-129 (cross-process reference rates). Trend across runs can reuse ctx.measures + measureHistory.

entries.rule: Percentage of incidents referencing a bare CI rather than a Business Service
entries.support_reason: The ratio is two counts over fields already extracted. The evidence "whether the referenced CIs have a traversable path to a service" needs a directed CI→service traversal; synthesize() has an undirected BFS and cmdb-signals traces service support, so the graph exists but not this query.
entries.volume_reason: Ratio is cheap; the traversal evidence touches the whole relationship table.

entries.rule: Incident assigned to a group with zero active members
entries.support_reason: Open incidents and their groups are already extracted; sys_user_grmember and sys_user are not in the allow-list and no batched membership resolution exists. Once members are read, the join is in-memory.
entries.volume_reason: Distinct referenced groups are few; membership rows are read for those groups only (sys_idIN batches).
entries.implementation_notes: Existing ITSM-INC-UNASSIGNED tests an EMPTY group field; this rule tests a group with no ACTIVE members — a different condition. Shares its resolver with ITSM-065, ITSM-101, ITSM-134.

entries.rule: Incident referencing a retired or non-existent CI
entries.support_reason: cmdb_ci is already read in full on every scan and cmdb-signals defines retired statuses (DQ_INACTIVE_INSTALL_STATUS), so the existence and state lookup is an in-memory join over extracted data; missing only the join utility and the two-case reporting.
entries.volume_reason: Depends on cmdb_ci being fully read — which the 100,000-row extraction cap makes impossible on a large CMDB; a dangling reference then cannot be distinguished from an unread CI.
entries.implementation_notes: "The live CI the incident probably concerns" evidence needs name matching (text analysis) — optional.

entries.rule: Resolution notes empty or below a meaningful length
entries.threshold_default: Length threshold default 20 characters after trimming
entries.support_reason: Resolved incidents with close_notes empty or trimmed length < 20 is a per-record predicate over incident fields; close_notes must be added to the extraction spec.
entries.volume_reason: close_notes is a large text field retrieved for every resolved incident in the slice.
entries.implementation_notes: Evidence "reopen rate for these versus properly documented" is an aggregate comparison — enrichment, not detection.

entries.rule: Resolution notes containing only a copy of the short description
entries.support_reason: Needs a string-similarity measure (threshold 0.9) per record; nothing in the codebase computes text similarity.
entries.volume_reason: Pairwise comparison within each record only (O(n)), but both text fields for every resolved incident.
entries.implementation_notes: Similarity metric is UNDEFINED by the workbook (only the threshold 0.9 is stated).

entries.rule: Caller field populated with a service account or generic user
entries.threshold_default: Volume threshold configurable; service account detection from naming and role pattern
entries.support_reason: Caller volume is one group-by; sys_user_has_role is already in the allow-list (Platform). Missing: sys_user read, the service-account classifier ("naming and role pattern" — UNDEFINED patterns) and a configurable volume threshold.
entries.volume_reason: Group-by caller, then resolve only high-volume callers.

entries.rule: Short description duplicated across large volumes (template pasting)
entries.threshold_default: Volume threshold configurable relative to total volume
entries.support_reason: Frequency of NORMALISED short descriptions needs text normalisation before counting; a raw group-by on short_description is possible via the Aggregate API but the workbook asks for normalised values.
entries.volume_reason: Every short_description in the slice is normalised and counted.
entries.implementation_notes: Normalisation rules UNDEFINED. Its output is an input to ITSM-058 (clusters diluted by template pasting).

entries.rule: Category not matching the resolution code pattern for that category
entries.threshold_default: Expected distribution derived from the estate's own data, minimum volume per category required
entries.support_reason: The joint distribution is one two-field group-by; the "expected joint distribution derived from the estate" and the outlier test ("far outside") are a statistical evaluator that does not exist, and the minimum volume per category is UNDEFINED.
entries.implementation_notes: The statistical test is not specified by the workbook (confidence 85%, "derived from the estate’s own patterns").

entries.rule: Close code and close notes inconsistent
entries.threshold_default: Consistency rules per close code, derived from the estate's own dominant patterns
entries.support_reason: Semantic consistency between free text and a code needs per-code expected note patterns derived from the estate and a consistency test; nothing comparable exists.
entries.implementation_notes: Workbook itself rates this the least certain rule (80%) and requires human validation before action.

entries.rule: Incident with no work notes at all through its lifecycle
entries.threshold_default: Any occurrence; report by group and priority
entries.support_reason: diagnostics.journalFor() reads journal entries for ONE record; counting work notes across every resolved incident needs a bulk journal read or an Aggregate API group-by on sys_journal_field.element_id.
entries.volume_reason: sys_journal_field is one of the largest tables on any instance; the count must be scoped to the incident slice.
entries.implementation_notes: Aggregate API: count sys_journal_field WHERE name=incident^element=work_notes GROUP BY element_id, then anti-join against resolved incidents.

entries.rule: Attachment-only resolution with no text record
entries.support_reason: Joins attachments to resolved incidents by table_sys_id and compares attachment time with resolution time within a window; no attachment reader and no time-window join utility.
entries.volume_reason: Only resolved incidents with empty close_notes need their attachments read.

entries.rule: Free-text fields containing PAN, Aadhaar, account numbers, or other identifiers (DPDP exposure)
entries.threshold_default: Pattern set per identifier type, with checksum validation where the format supports it
entries.support_reason: A regex pattern set with per-type checksum validation (Luhn, Verhoeff for Aadhaar) over free text, reporting counts and locations only — no content scanner exists. The ACL-state evidence can reuse servicenow/acl.js.
entries.volume_reason: Every free-text field and every journal entry in scope.
entries.implementation_notes: Evidence contract: COUNT AND LOCATION ONLY — matched values must never be stored or rendered. This constrains the finding/evidence shape (no field_value).

entries.rule: Location or department unpopulated where routing depends on it
entries.threshold_default: Fires only where routing rules reference the fields
entries.support_reason: Fires only where a routing rule evaluates the field, so it needs the assignment-rule reader (as ITSM-004); the record half is a plain predicate.
entries.volume_reason: Predicate over the slice, gated by configuration.

entries.rule: Reopen rate above threshold, by group and by resolution code
entries.support_reason: reopen_count is already extracted and the existing ITSM-INC-REOPENED predicate reads it; the ratio by group/code is a group-by. The workbook specifies reopen detection FROM STATE AUDIT and time-to-reopen distribution, which need bulk sys_audit.
entries.volume_reason: Ratio via counts is cheap; time-to-reopen needs audit rows for every reopened incident.
entries.implementation_notes: Thresholds: 8% (escalate above 15%). Dependents: ITSM-007 and ITSM-031 both describe suppressing this rule.

entries.rule: Auto-close used as the primary closure mechanism (resolution never verified)
configuration_objects: auto-close job attribution (UNDEFINED — which user/job closes; commonly closed_by = system)
entries.support_reason: COUNT(auto-closed)/COUNT(closed) is a group-by on closed_by once the auto-close attribution is defined; the attribution itself is UNDEFINED by the workbook.
entries.implementation_notes: Threshold 70%. "Caller confirmation rate where captured" — UNDEFINED source.

entries.rule: Reassignment count distribution with a long tail (ticket ping-pong)
entries.support_reason: The tail of reassignment_count is a group-by/histogram on a field (needs adding to the spec). The group-pair transition matrix needs assignment_group audit history for the tail population — bulk sys_audit.
entries.volume_reason: Histogram is cheap; the transition matrix reads audit rows for every tail incident.
entries.implementation_notes: Tail threshold 4.

entries.rule: SLA breach rate above threshold
entries.threshold_default: Threshold from the customer's own commitment; default 10%
entries.support_reason: diagnostics.slasFor() reads task_sla for one task; a breach ratio by definition/group/priority is an Aggregate API group-by on task_sla (not in the allow-list) joined to incident for group/priority.
entries.volume_reason: task_sla holds several rows per task; group-by keeps it cheap, the join to incident for group/priority does not.
entries.implementation_notes: Workbook: only valid once ITSM-003 and ITSM-012 are resolved; report them alongside. Threshold default 10% or the customer commitment.

entries.rule: SLA paused or cancelled at abnormal rates (gaming)
entries.threshold_default: Default flag at 2x the estate mean rate
entries.support_reason: Pause/cancel EVENT rates need task_sla stage transitions (audit) or at least task_sla pause_duration vs business_duration per row, compared with the estate mean per group/definition; no bulk task_sla read and no rate-vs-mean evaluator.
entries.volume_reason: task_sla rows plus their audit history for every incident in the slice.
entries.implementation_notes: Threshold 2x the estate mean rate. "Pause reasons where captured" — UNDEFINED field.

entries.rule: Resolution time distribution with a spike immediately before SLA expiry
entries.threshold_default: Spike threshold default 2x the expected density for that interval
entries.support_reason: Histogram of (resolved_at − planned_end_time) per incident needs a join of every resolved incident to its resolution task_sla, then a density test in the final decile against an expected distribution — neither the join nor the density evaluator exists.
entries.volume_reason: Row-level join incident × task_sla over the slice.
entries.implementation_notes: Spike threshold 2x expected density; the expected distribution is UNDEFINED (uniform? estate-derived?).

entries.rule: Incidents resolved and closed within seconds of creation (bulk closure)
entries.support_reason: create-to-close < 60 s is timestamp arithmetic over incident fields (closed_at, closed_by need adding to the spec); grouping by closing user and time window is presentation over the same rows.
entries.volume_reason: Every closed incident in the slice; an encoded query cannot express a field-to-field interval, so row-level.
entries.implementation_notes: "Clustered in bursts" evidence is a time-bucketed count — aggregate presentation.

entries.rule: Backlog ageing beyond threshold by priority
entries.threshold_default: Age thresholds per priority; defaults 2 days P1, 5 days P2, 15 days P3
entries.support_reason: Open-incident age against a per-priority threshold is a per-record predicate over fields already extracted; the existing ITSM-INC-P1-AGED is the P1 case with a 1-day threshold. The trend needs measures history (pattern exists).
entries.implementation_notes: Defaults 2d P1, 5d P2, 15d P3; P4/P5 UNDEFINED. Existing hard-coded rule uses 1 day for P1 — a threshold conflict to resolve in a later phase, not here.

entries.rule: P1 raised manually where automated conditions existed
entries.support_reason: Correlates manually created P1s with alerts in the preceding window by CI and time; em_alert is in the allow-list (ITOM) but no time-window correlation exists. "Creation source" (manual vs automated) is UNDEFINED — contact_type or sys_created_by.
entries.volume_reason: P1s are few; alerts in the preceding window per P1.
entries.implementation_notes: Alert rule state evidence needs em_alert rule configuration — UNDEFINED table.

entries.rule: P1 volume without corresponding Problem records
entries.support_reason: incident.problem_id is a field on incident (add to spec), so "P1 with no linked Problem" is a predicate plus a ratio; verifying the referenced Problem exists is an in-memory join over extracted problems.
entries.implementation_notes: Threshold 30%. "Recurrence pattern among unanalysed P1s" evidence needs text clustering (ITSM-054 family).

entries.rule: Incidents created by the same caller repeatedly for the same issue (unresolved root cause)
entries.threshold_default: Similarity threshold and repeat count configurable
entries.support_reason: Clusters descriptions by similarity per caller and counts repeats above a threshold — needs the clustering capability.
entries.volume_reason: Clustering within each caller’s incidents; bounded per caller but across the whole slice.
entries.implementation_notes: Similarity threshold and repeat count UNDEFINED defaults.

entries.rule: First-call resolution rate declining
entries.support_reason: FCR = resolved with reassignment_count = 0 is two counts; the TREND across at least three windows needs either per-window counts in one run (sys_created_on buckets) or run-to-run measures history (ctx.measures / measureHistory exists for CMDB-038).

entries.rule: Assignment to an individual rather than a group
entries.threshold_default: Report as a ratio and by individual
entries.support_reason: assigned_to populated with assignment_group empty is a predicate over fields already in the incident spec; ratio and by-individual breakdown are presentation.
entries.implementation_notes: The second clause "assignment patterns concentrated on individuals" is a distribution (aggregate) with an UNDEFINED concentration threshold.

entries.rule: On-hold reason not captured
entries.threshold_default: Any occurrence; report as a ratio
entries.support_reason: "On-hold transitions with empty hold reason" is an event, not a state: it needs the state-change audit row and the hold_reason value at that moment. A weaker current-state form (state=On Hold AND hold_reason empty) is a record predicate, but is not what the workbook specifies.
entries.volume_reason: State transitions from sys_audit for every incident in the slice.
entries.implementation_notes: Makes ITSM-034 uninterpretable when high; SLA pause attribution evidence needs task_sla.

entries.rule: Incidents resolved by the caller themselves
entries.threshold_default: Report separately for callers with and without fulfiller roles
entries.support_reason: caller_id = resolved_by is a predicate (resolved_by needs adding); the role-set join uses sys_user_has_role, already extracted for the Platform module. Missing: a definition of "fulfiller roles" (UNDEFINED) and the join utility.
entries.volume_reason: Resolved incidents; role rows for the matching callers only.

entries.rule: No major incident process configured despite P1 volume
configuration_objects: major incident configuration (UNDEFINED — Major Incident Management plugin state/properties)
entries.support_reason: P1 volume is a count; "major incident records" and "configuration state" depend on the MIM plugin (candidate: incident.major_incident_state) with no reader and no plugin-presence probe.
entries.implementation_notes: P1 volume threshold UNDEFINED. Evidence "P1s that met MI criteria by duration or impact" needs the criteria (ITSM-051).

entries.rule: Major incident raised with no communication plan or task
entries.support_reason: Communication plan / communication task records are MIM plugin objects the workbook does not name (UNDEFINED tables); no reader exists.

entries.rule: Major incident closed with no post-incident review
entries.support_reason: Post-incident review linkage is a MIM plugin object (UNDEFINED table); no reader.

entries.rule: Major incident with no linked Problem record
entries.support_reason: Problem linkage is incident.problem_id (in-memory join over extracted problems, as ITSM-039); identifying major incidents needs the MIM state field (candidate major_incident_state, plugin-dependent).

entries.rule: Major incident with no affected service populated
entries.support_reason: The predicate (MI with no service reference) is a record check once major incidents are identifiable; the evidence "traversable path to a service" needs the directed CI→service traversal (as ITSM-017) — and the Lane 1 remediation depends on it.
entries.volume_reason: Major incidents only; traversal per MI.

entries.rule: Major incident timeline gaps (no updates for extended periods)
entries.threshold_default: Gap threshold default 30 minutes during an active major incident
entries.support_reason: Gap analysis over the journal timeline of each major incident; journalFor() reads one record’s journal (with a limit) and the MI identification is plugin-dependent.
entries.volume_reason: Few major incidents, but each needs its full journal.

entries.rule: Major incident candidate criteria never triggering
entries.threshold_default: Any occurrence with qualifying P1s present
entries.support_reason: Candidate criteria, trigger events and manual promotion records are all MIM plugin objects with no reader; evaluating "P1s that met the criteria" needs the criteria to be executable.

entries.rule: Post-incident review actions created but never closed
entries.support_reason: The predicate (open action older than 90 days) is trivial, but the PIR action table is UNDEFINED (MIM plugin) and not readable through any existing path.
entries.implementation_notes: "Whether that incident type has recurred since" evidence needs clustering.

entries.rule: Problem process effectively unused — Problem-to-Incident ratio near zero
entries.support_reason: Two counts over already-extracted tables (created in the window); missing the ratio evaluator with a two-tier threshold (0.5%, escalate below 0.1%) and the trend.
entries.implementation_notes: Evidence "incident clusters that should have produced Problems" is ITSM-054’s output.

entries.rule: Recurring incident patterns with no corresponding Problem record
entries.threshold_default: Cluster volume threshold and similarity threshold configurable
entries.support_reason: Clustering incidents by description and category similarity, then checking Problem linkage per cluster — the clustering capability does not exist.
entries.volume_reason: Similarity clustering across the whole incident slice is quadratic unless blocked by category.
entries.implementation_notes: Cluster volume and similarity thresholds UNDEFINED defaults. Depends on ITSM-002 (category taxonomy) per the workbook cross-link.

entries.rule: P1 and major incidents with no Problem raised
entries.threshold_default: Any occurrence; report as a ratio
entries.support_reason: P1 half is a predicate + in-memory join on problem_id; the major-incident half is plugin-dependent (as ITSM-048).

entries.rule: Problem records created but never progressed past initial state
entries.support_reason: Problems in the initial state older than 30 days is a predicate over extracted problem rows (initial state value UNDEFINED — first choice? OOB "New"?); the workbook additionally requires "no state change" from audit, which needs bulk sys_audit for problems (few rows, so per-record auditFor() could serve as a bridge).
entries.volume_reason: Problems are few; audit rows per problem.

entries.rule: Percentage of incident volume attributable to known problems
entries.threshold_default: Report by Problem state; no single threshold
entries.support_reason: COUNT(linked)/COUNT(all) is a count on problem_idISNOTEMPTY; the split by Problem state is an in-memory join to extracted problems. "Effort each represents" needs resolution-time sums (Aggregate API avg/sum not wrapped).
entries.volume_reason: Counts plus a join on the linked subset.
entries.implementation_notes: No single threshold — reported by state.

entries.rule: Top ten incident clusters by short-description similarity with no Problem
entries.threshold_default: N default 10; effort derived from resolution time
entries.support_reason: Top-N similarity clusters ranked by aggregate resolution effort — clustering plus effort arithmetic; nothing exists.
entries.volume_reason: Same clustering cost as ITSM-054 plus per-cluster effort.
entries.implementation_notes: N default 10. Workbook: clusters are diluted by ITSM-023 template pasting — report alongside.

entries.rule: Problem raised only by one group (process not adopted estate-wide)
entries.threshold_default: Flag where Problem creation concentration far exceeds incident concentration
entries.support_reason: Two group-bys (problem creation by group, incident volume by group) and a per-group ratio comparison; the "far exceeds" threshold is UNDEFINED.

entries.rule: Problem records with no linked incidents
entries.support_reason: Zero linked incidents is an anti-join of problems against a group-by count of incident.problem_id — both tables are extracted; missing the join utility. Lane 1 evidence "incident clusters that match their description" needs text analysis.
entries.volume_reason: Problems are few; one group-by on incident.
entries.implementation_notes: Note the incident slice is 90 days: linkage to older incidents is invisible unless the count is taken via Aggregate API over all incidents.

entries.rule: Problems open beyond age threshold with no state change
entries.support_reason: As ITSM-056 with a 90-day threshold on open problems; "no state change beyond age threshold" needs the last state-change timestamp from audit (per-record auditFor() bridge for the small problem population).
entries.implementation_notes: Existing ITSM-PRB-STALE uses sys_updated_on (any update) with 30 days — a different definition from "no STATE change" in 90 days.

entries.rule: Root cause field empty on closed Problems
entries.threshold_default: Any occurrence; report as a ratio
entries.support_reason: Closed problems with empty root cause is a predicate over problem fields (cause_notes / close code need adding to the spec).
entries.implementation_notes: Which field is "root cause" (cause_notes vs a custom field) must be confirmed per instance. Post-closure incident trend evidence needs linkage + windows.

entries.rule: Workaround empty on Problems with open linked incidents
entries.support_reason: Problem with empty workaround AND ≥1 open linked incident is a join between the two extracted tables; missing the join utility and the workaround field in the spec.

entries.rule: Problem closed with no permanent fix and no accepted-risk decision
entries.support_reason: problem.rfc (linked change) and problem.known_error are fields on problem (add to spec); "accepted-risk record" is UNDEFINED (no OOB field — instance-specific), so the third leg of the predicate cannot be defined.

entries.rule: Problem with no assigned owner, or owner inactive
entries.support_reason: Same resolver as ITSM-018 applied to problem.assigned_to (user active) and assignment_group (active members); the existing ITSM-PRB-UNASSIGNED covers only the empty-group case.

entries.rule: Known Error records not published to knowledge
entries.support_reason: Known Error → knowledge article linkage: the link field is UNDEFINED by the workbook (OOB is a m2m or kb_knowledge reference depending on version); kb_knowledge is not readable through any existing path.

entries.rule: Problem not linked to a CI or service
entries.threshold_default: Any occurrence; report as a ratio
entries.support_reason: Both references empty is a predicate over problem fields (business_service needs adding to the spec).
entries.implementation_notes: Lane 1 evidence "the CI the linked incidents point at" is a join to incidents — enrichment.

entries.rule: Problem tasks created but never completed
entries.support_reason: Trivial age predicate, but "Problem task records" (candidate problem_task) is not in the allow-list.

entries.rule: Problem closed while linked incidents remain open
entries.support_reason: Closed problems with ≥1 open linked incident — a join over the two extracted tables (needs the join utility and problem_id in the incident spec).

entries.rule: Root cause text below meaningful length or restating the symptom
entries.threshold_default: Length threshold default 40 characters; similarity threshold 0.85
entries.support_reason: The length half (< 40 chars) is a predicate; the similarity half (0.85 vs description) needs the similarity measure.

entries.rule: Problem with no linked Change where a fix was clearly required
entries.threshold_default: Root cause classification from close code and text pattern
entries.support_reason: Root cause CLASSIFICATION from close code and text pattern ("indicating a configuration or code fix") is a text classifier with UNDEFINED patterns; the linkage half (problem.rfc empty) is simple.
entries.implementation_notes: Evidence "unauthorised change detected on the related CI in the window" is ITSM-106’s output.

entries.rule: Problem state regressing repeatedly
entries.support_reason: "Backward" state transitions need the ordered state audit per problem AND an ordering of states (UNDEFINED — which transitions are backward); no state-order model exists.
entries.implementation_notes: Default 2 backward transitions.

entries.rule: Problem priority not aligned to the aggregate impact of linked incidents
entries.support_reason: Aggregate linked-incident priority per problem is a join + group-by over extracted tables; the "alignment matrix" is configurable with no default (UNDEFINED), so the comparison cannot be specified.

entries.rule: Incident volume for a resolved Problem not declining post-closure (fix ineffective)
entries.threshold_default: Window default 90 days either side. Flag where the decline is below threshold.
entries.support_reason: Before/after incident rate per closed problem needs two windowed counts anchored on each problem’s closure date — a per-record temporal window over incidents beyond the 90-day slice (needs Aggregate API per problem or a 180-day incident read).
entries.volume_reason: Two counts per closed problem in scope.
entries.implementation_notes: Decline threshold UNDEFINED. Must not evaluate before the full post-closure window has elapsed (workbook FPG).

entries.rule: Problem recurrence — same root cause appearing in multiple Problem records
entries.threshold_default: Similarity threshold default 0.8, minimum cluster size 2
entries.support_reason: Clustering problems by root-cause text similarity (0.8, min cluster 2).
entries.volume_reason: Problems are few — clustering is tractable here.

entries.rule: Known Error articles with no views or no linkage from incidents
entries.support_reason: Known-error article views and incident→article linkage (UNDEFINED link: m2m_kb_task) — no kb_knowledge reader and no linkage table in the allow-list.

entries.rule: Average time from incident cluster emergence to Problem creation
entries.threshold_default: Report distribution, not a single threshold
entries.support_reason: Needs the clusters from ITSM-054/058 (text analysis), their first-occurrence dates, and the linked Problem creation date — a distribution over cluster→problem intervals.
entries.implementation_notes: No threshold — distribution reported.

entries.rule: Permanent fix implemented but no validation recorded
entries.support_reason: Fix recorded (fix_notes) with linked change closure is a join over extracted tables; "validation entry / post-implementation review" is UNDEFINED as a field or record, so half the predicate is unspecified.

entries.rule: Problems closed as "cannot reproduce" above threshold
entries.support_reason: A ratio by group over one field (problem close code — field name per instance; add to spec) with a 20% threshold; missing the ratio evaluator.
entries.implementation_notes: Which close code value means "cannot reproduce" is instance-specific.

entries.rule: Standard change catalogue empty or unused — everything routed as Normal
entries.threshold_default: Default threshold 20% of changes as standard for a mature estate
entries.support_reason: type distribution is a group-by on an already-extracted field; the template count/usage needs the standard-change template table (not in the allow-list, plugin-dependent). Evidence "Normal changes with repeated identical descriptions" needs text frequency (ITSM-023 family).
entries.volume_reason: One group-by plus a small template table.
entries.implementation_notes: Threshold 20% standard for a mature estate.

entries.rule: Approval routing with no defined approver group for a change type
configuration_objects: change approval workflow configuration by type (UNDEFINED — flow or workflow definitions)
entries.support_reason: Approval routing configuration lives in flows/workflows/approval rules with no reader that can say "which approver group applies to type X". Volume per type is a group-by (reusable). Actual approval records (sysapproval_approver) are not in the allow-list.
entries.volume_reason: Configuration plus approvals for the type.

entries.rule: CAB not configured, or CAB meeting workflow unused
entries.support_reason: CAB Workbench tables are plugin-dependent and unread; change volume in the window is reusable.

entries.rule: Risk assessment not configured, or risk always computed as the same value
configuration_objects: risk assessment configuration and questionnaire completion (UNDEFINED — Change Risk Assessment plugin tables)
entries.support_reason: Risk value distribution is a group-by on change_request.risk (add to spec) with an 80% dominance threshold; the "unconfigured" branch and questionnaire completion are plugin objects with no reader. Correlation of risk vs failure rate is a second group-by (risk × close_code).

entries.rule: No conflict detection configured
configuration_objects: conflict detection configuration (UNDEFINED — properties / conflict table)
entries.threshold_default: Report both cases; the second is ITSM-138
entries.support_reason: Configuration state (no reader) plus a schedule-overlap analysis of changes on the same or related CIs (temporal correlation over the relationship graph) to show conflicts existed and were not detected.
entries.volume_reason: Pairwise window overlap across changes on related CIs.
entries.implementation_notes: The workbook says the second case IS ITSM-138 — the two rules share the overlap analysis; both stay independent.

entries.rule: Blackout and maintenance windows not defined
configuration_objects: blackout and maintenance window definitions (cmn_schedule, type = blackout / maintenance)
entries.support_reason: sla.js slaMeta() already reads cmn_schedule; missing: filtering by schedule type for blackout/maintenance and the change-volume-by-date evidence.
entries.implementation_notes: Precondition for ITSM-112 and ITSM-127.

entries.rule: Emergency change path with the same approval requirements as Normal (so it gets bypassed)
entries.threshold_default: Flag where emergency approval burden is not materially lighter
entries.support_reason: Comparing emergency vs normal approval STEP COUNTS needs the approval configuration reader (as ITSM-081); turnaround by type needs approval records (sysapproval_approver) with timestamps.
entries.volume_reason: Approvals for changes in the window.
entries.implementation_notes: "Not materially lighter" threshold UNDEFINED.

entries.rule: Change model states allowing closure without implementation evidence
configuration_objects: change model state/closure requirements (candidate chg_model, chg_model_state, plus UI/data policies)
entries.support_reason: Change model closure requirements and mandatory-field policies have no reader; the "proportion of closed changes with no implementation evidence" half is a count (close_notesISEMPTY) that is reusable.
entries.implementation_notes: "Implementation evidence fields" UNDEFINED beyond close_notes.

entries.rule: Approval delegation configured to inactive users
entries.support_reason: Delegate → sys_user.active is the same user-state resolver as ITSM-018/065; the delegation table is not in the allow-list, and "approvals currently hanging on it" needs sysapproval_approver.

entries.rule: Standard change templates with no expiry or review date
entries.threshold_default: Review period from policy; default 12 months
entries.support_reason: Simple predicate, but on a plugin table with UNDEFINED expiry/review fields (the OOB standard-change template has no review date field; instance-specific).
entries.implementation_notes: Evidence "success rate for changes raised from each" is a join to change_request.std_change_producer_version × close_code.

entries.rule: Risk matrix fields not mandatory
configuration_objects: risk matrix input field mandatory configuration (dictionary mandatory flag; UI/data policies)
entries.support_reason: dba-schema getField() reads dictionary.mandatory; population rate per field is a count. Missing: UI/data-policy mandatory state (no reader) and the definition of "risk matrix input fields" (UNDEFINED — risk/impact? plugin questionnaire?).
entries.implementation_notes: Population threshold 80%. Root cause of ITSM-083 per the workbook.

entries.rule: Change types customised without corresponding approval logic
configuration_objects: change type choices vs OOB set (OOB baseline UNDEFINED)
approval workflow coverage by type (UNDEFINED reader)
entries.threshold_default: Any custom type with non-zero volume
entries.support_reason: Choice list and volume per type are reusable; "no matching approval workflow condition" needs the approval configuration reader (as ITSM-081) and an OOB type baseline.

entries.rule: No post-implementation review step for high-risk changes
configuration_objects: change model PIR configuration by risk band (UNDEFINED)
entries.support_reason: Both the PIR step configuration and PIR records are UNDEFINED objects; high-risk change volume is a count (reusable). Incident-rate-following evidence is ITSM-115/123 output.
entries.implementation_notes: Risk bands configurable — UNDEFINED default.

entries.rule: Change calendar not published or not consumed
configuration_objects: calendar view access logs where available (UNDEFINED — likely unavailable over REST)
entries.threshold_default: Access threshold where log data is available
entries.support_reason: Neither the calendar configuration nor access logs are identifiable platform tables; consumption evidence is explicitly conditional on log availability.
entries.implementation_notes: Access threshold UNDEFINED; the workbook itself makes consumption evidence conditional.

entries.rule: Percentage of changes with no CI and no service reference
entries.support_reason: Same shape as ITSM-016 on change_request (business_service must be added to the change spec; the existing ITSM-CHG-NO-CI tests cmdb_ci only); ratio, 30% threshold and trend are missing.
entries.implementation_notes: Workbook: makes ITSM-084 and ITSM-138 structurally impossible when high; ITSM-106 and ITSM-123 understate when high. Feeds ITSM-129.

entries.rule: Change referencing a retired or non-existent CI
entries.support_reason: As ITSM-019 on change_request — in-memory join against the fully extracted cmdb_ci, subject to the same extraction-cap caveat.
entries.volume_reason: Depends on a complete cmdb_ci read.

entries.rule: Implementation plan empty
entries.threshold_default: Any occurrence; report by type and risk band
entries.support_reason: Approved-or-closed changes with empty implementation_plan is a predicate over change fields (implementation_plan, approval, risk need adding to the spec).
entries.volume_reason: implementation_plan is a large text field retrieved for the whole slice.
entries.implementation_notes: An encoded query (implementation_planISEMPTY) can push the predicate server-side. "Approval records showing what was approved" evidence needs sysapproval_approver.

entries.rule: Backout plan empty
entries.threshold_default: Any occurrence; escalate for high-risk and production changes
entries.support_reason: As ITSM-096 for backout_plan.
entries.volume_reason: Large text field over the slice; pushable as backout_planISEMPTY.
entries.implementation_notes: "Escalate for high-risk and production changes" — production is a CI-context escalator (cmdb-signals).

entries.rule: Test plan empty on high-risk changes
entries.support_reason: High-risk changes with empty test_plan — predicate over change fields (test_plan, risk to add). "High-risk" band is configurable (UNDEFINED default).

entries.rule: Risk and impact fields unpopulated
entries.support_reason: Risk or impact empty at approval — predicate over change fields; "at approval" is approximated by approval/state = approved (the approval moment itself is history).

entries.rule: Planned start and end dates absent or in the past at approval
entries.threshold_default: Report the two cases separately; the second feeds ITSM-108
entries.support_reason: Empty planned dates on approved changes is a predicate over extracted fields; "planned start earlier than approval date" needs the approval TIMESTAMP, which is not a change_request field (sysapproval_approver.sys_updated_on or audit).
entries.volume_reason: Approved changes plus their approval rows.
entries.implementation_notes: Second case feeds ITSM-108.

entries.rule: Assignment group with zero active members
entries.support_reason: Same resolver as ITSM-018 applied to open changes.
entries.volume_reason: Open changes; membership for referenced groups.

entries.rule: Justification or business reason empty
entries.support_reason: Approved-or-closed changes with empty justification — predicate over change fields (justification / reason to add).
entries.volume_reason: Text field over the slice; pushable as justificationISEMPTY.
entries.implementation_notes: Which of justification / reason is the "business reason" field is instance-specific.

entries.rule: Change closed with no close code or close notes
entries.support_reason: Closed changes with empty close_code or close_notes, two cases — predicate over change fields (close_code already in the spec; close_notes to add).
entries.implementation_notes: Corrupts ITSM-113 when high.

entries.rule: Backout plan text identical across many changes (template pasting)
entries.threshold_default: Volume threshold configurable relative to change volume
entries.support_reason: Normalised-text frequency over backout_plan — the same normalisation + frequency capability ITSM-023 needs.
entries.volume_reason: backout_plan text for every change in the slice.

entries.rule: Affected CI list containing a single CI where the change clearly spans more
entries.threshold_default: Scope inference from change type and CI relationship depth
entries.support_reason: Dependent CIs of the primary CI can come from the existing relationship graph (synthesize builds it); the affected-CI list (task_ci) is not in the allow-list, and "description or type indicates broader scope" is a text/type heuristic with UNDEFINED rules.
entries.volume_reason: Graph traversal per change with a single affected CI.

entries.rule: Unauthorised change rate — CI modified with no corresponding approved change
entries.threshold_default: Scope to change-controlled object classes; correlation window configurable
entries.support_reason: Configuration-object modifications from sys_audit (bulk, scoped to change-controlled classes — UNDEFINED which) matched against approved change windows on the same object: bulk audit read plus a time-window join, neither of which exists.
entries.volume_reason: sys_audit over every change-controlled object in the window.
entries.implementation_notes: Workbook: understates where ITSM-094 is high; state the understatement. cmdb_ci is not audited on dev424910 (ARCHITECTURE §16.8) — attribution may be impossible on some instances.

entries.rule: Emergency change ratio above threshold (emergency used to bypass control)
entries.support_reason: Emergency ratio overall and by group is a group-by on type (already extracted); "by approver" needs approval records (sysapproval_approver, not in the allow-list).
entries.volume_reason: Group-bys plus approvals for emergency changes.
entries.implementation_notes: Thresholds 10% / escalate above 25%.

entries.rule: Retrospective change rate — changes raised after implementation
entries.threshold_default: Correlation against CI audit where available; otherwise against actual start field
entries.support_reason: The 80%-confidence path (creation/approval timestamp after work_start) is a predicate over change fields plus the approval timestamp (as ITSM-100); the 95% path corroborates with CI audit (bulk sys_audit — missing).
entries.volume_reason: Changes plus approvals; VERY_HIGH if CI audit corroboration is used.

entries.rule: Self-approval — requester and approver the same person
entries.support_reason: Direct comparison requested_by = approver, but approver lives on approval records (sysapproval_approver.approver, document_id) — no reader and not in the allow-list.
entries.volume_reason: Approval rows for changes in the window.

entries.rule: Approval granted outside the approver's authority level
configuration_objects: approver authority matrix — from the customer’s delegation policy (UNDEFINED; external input)
entries.threshold_default: Authority matrix from the customer's own delegation policy
entries.support_reason: Needs approval records plus an authority matrix the workbook says must come from the customer; where none exists, the rule reports that absence.

entries.rule: Change implemented outside its approved window
entries.support_reason: Actual window (work_start/work_end) outside the planned window beyond tolerance — timestamp arithmetic over change fields (work_start/work_end to add). The CI-audit inference path (90%) is an alternative needing audit.
entries.implementation_notes: Evidence "conflicting change in the actual window" is the overlap analysis (ITSM-084/138).

entries.rule: Change implemented during a blackout period
entries.threshold_default: Requires blackout windows to be defined; report ITSM-085 where they are not
entries.support_reason: Blackout definitions are readable via the cmn_schedule path sla.js uses; missing: schedule SPAN expansion (recurring spans → concrete intervals) and the interval-intersection test per change.
entries.implementation_notes: Override justification evidence — UNDEFINED field.

entries.rule: Change success rate below threshold
entries.support_reason: Success ratio by type/risk/group is a group-by on close_code (already extracted; existing ITSM-CHG-FAILED reads it); missing the ratio evaluator, 90% threshold and trend.
entries.implementation_notes: Workbook: requires ITSM-103 and ITSM-115 to interpret.

entries.rule: Failed change rate with no corresponding backout executed
entries.support_reason: Failed changes are a predicate on close_code (extracted); backout task completion needs change_task (not in the allow-list) — "backout evidence recorded" is otherwise UNDEFINED.

entries.rule: Changes closed as Successful with a linked incident created within the window
entries.threshold_default: Window default 72 hours. CI correlation includes dependent CIs where relationships exist.
entries.support_reason: Join successful changes to incidents on the same or dependent CI within 72 h of implementation — a CI+time-window correlation over the relationship graph; no such join exists.
entries.volume_reason: Changes × incidents by CI with graph expansion.
entries.implementation_notes: Same correlation kernel as ITSM-123/124/125/128. Feeds ITSM-124; corrects ITSM-113.

entries.rule: Approval turnaround near-zero (rubber-stamping)
entries.threshold_default: Default threshold 120 seconds. Report the distribution, not only the outliers.
entries.support_reason: Turnaround = approval timestamp − request timestamp per approval record, distributed by approver — needs sysapproval_approver reads and a distribution evaluator.
entries.implementation_notes: Threshold 120 s; report the distribution, not only outliers.

entries.rule: Standard change used for work that meets Normal change criteria
entries.threshold_default: Template scope from the template definition
entries.support_reason: Template scope (plugin table), actual affected CIs (task_ci), risk indicators and DESCRIPTION comparison against the template — configuration + linkage + text analysis in sequence.

entries.rule: Conflict detected but overridden with no justification
entries.support_reason: Conflict results, override records and the justification field are all UNDEFINED objects (candidate conflict table); no reader.

entries.rule: Change with no linked incident or problem and no business justification
entries.support_reason: Empty justification is a field predicate; "no linked incident and no linked problem" depends on how linkage is modelled on the instance (change_request.parent, or task_rel_task m2m — UNDEFINED), so the linkage leg may need a relationship table.

entries.rule: Changes repeatedly rescheduled
entries.support_reason: Reschedule count = number of audit rows on planned date fields per change — an Aggregate API group-by on sys_audit (documentkey) or bulk audit read; neither exists.
entries.volume_reason: sys_audit rows for date fields across the change slice; a group-by count keeps it tractable.
entries.implementation_notes: Default 3 reschedules. "Whether conflict detection was re-run after each" is UNDEFINED.

entries.rule: Approvals by a single approver across a disproportionate share of changes
entries.support_reason: Share of approvals per approver is one group-by — on a table with no reader and outside the allow-list.
entries.implementation_notes: Threshold 25% of total approvals.

entries.rule: Change closed without post-implementation review where required
entries.support_reason: PIR records and the PIR-required-by-band configuration are UNDEFINED objects (as ITSM-092).

entries.rule: Percentage of P1 incidents preceded by a change on the same CI within the window
entries.threshold_default: Window default 72 hours. Dependent CI traversal depth default 2.
entries.support_reason: P1 incidents matched to preceding changes on the same or dependent CI (depth 2) within 72 h — the CI+time correlation kernel with graph expansion; the undirected BFS in synthesize() is reusable for expansion but nothing joins by time.
entries.volume_reason: P1s are few, but each needs the change set on its CI neighbourhood in the window.
entries.implementation_notes: The headline change-quality measure; 124, 125 inherit its confidence. Denominator unreliable where ITSM-094 is high.

entries.rule: Change-induced incident rate by group, by type, by CI class
entries.threshold_default: Same window and traversal parameters as ITSM-123
entries.support_reason: Consumes ITSM-123’s correlated pairs and re-aggregates by group, type and CI class with a minimum volume per dimension — requires inter-rule output passing.
entries.volume_reason: Inherits ITSM-123, extended from P1s to all correlated incidents.
entries.implementation_notes: Minimum volume per dimension UNDEFINED.

entries.rule: CIs with a repeated change-then-incident pattern
entries.support_reason: Counts correlated pairs per CI (from ITSM-123/124 output), flags > 3, normalised by change volume per CI, and checks Problem existence for the CI.
entries.implementation_notes: Default 3 occurrences; normalise by change volume (FPG).

entries.rule: Changes to CIs supporting Business Critical services with no service reference populated
entries.support_reason: cmdb-signals already traces which CIs support a Business Critical service (buildSignals); missing: applying it to change CIs (and affected CIs via task_ci) and the business_service field in the change spec. Lane 1 remediation reuses the health proposal path (FIX_FIELD on change_request.business_service).
entries.volume_reason: Traversal per change; depends on complete cmdb_rel_ci.
entries.implementation_notes: Traversal depth configurable — UNDEFINED default.

entries.rule: Change freeze periods with change activity anyway
configuration_objects: freeze period definitions (UNDEFINED — cmn_schedule type, or a change-freeze table)
entries.threshold_default: Requires freeze periods to be defined
entries.support_reason: Same interval-intersection as ITSM-112 with freeze periods instead of blackouts; the freeze definition source is UNDEFINED and "freeze exception approvals" have no defined object.

entries.rule: Incidents resolved with a resolution code indicating change causation, but no change linked
entries.time_window: preceding window (UNDEFINED default) for the evidence
entries.support_reason: incident.rfc (caused-by change) empty with a change-causation close code is a predicate (close code set configurable — UNDEFINED default; fields to add). The evidence "changes in the preceding window on the same CI" is the correlation kernel (ITSM-123).
entries.volume_reason: Resolved incidents with the given codes.
entries.implementation_notes: Understates ITSM-123/124 when high.

entries.rule: Incident, Problem and Change all failing to reference the CMDB — the three processes operating blind
entries.threshold_default: Per-process thresholds; fires only when all three breach
entries.support_reason: Three reference-rate ratios (ITSM-016, ITSM-094 and the problem equivalent) evaluated together with per-process thresholds; the ratios are cheap counts over extracted tables, but "fires only when all three breach" needs rule-output composition and the CMDB Trust Score context (cmdb_quality exists in the manifest).
entries.implementation_notes: Per-process thresholds UNDEFINED (the individual rules state 40% / 30% / none).

entries.rule: Incident volume on CIs with no relationships (impact analysis structurally impossible)
entries.support_reason: Edge count per CI is derivable from the extracted cmdb_rel_ci (the existing CMDB-UNRELATED rule computes exactly "zero edges"); joining incident volume per CI and the 25% ratio is missing.
entries.volume_reason: Depends on a complete cmdb_rel_ci read; incidents group-by cmdb_ci is cheap.

entries.rule: Change risk assessment computed without CMDB dependency data
entries.support_reason: Relationship depth of the affected CIs comes from the existing graph; the risk value is a change field (to add); the risk calculation configuration (to show risk WAS computed from dependency data) is UNDEFINED. Failure-rate comparison is a group-by.
entries.implementation_notes: Depth threshold UNDEFINED.

entries.rule: Recurring incidents on CIs whose CMDB data is stale, traced to a discovery failure
entries.threshold_default: Requires the ITOM cause to be identified; links to ITOM-147
entries.support_reason: Recurring incident clusters per CI (text clustering) on CIs whose staleness (CMDB-STALE / cmdb-signals) traces to an identified Discovery failure (ITOM findings DISC-*) — three domains’ outputs chained.

entries.rule: Business Critical service with high incident volume and no Problem records
entries.threshold_default: Volume threshold relative to the service population
entries.support_reason: Services and criticality are already extracted (cmdb_ci_service); incident volume per service is a group-by; problem linkage by service is a join to extracted problems (business_service to add). Missing the join/threshold; "volume threshold relative to the service population" is UNDEFINED.
entries.implementation_notes: FPG: problems raised against CIs rather than the service — needs CI→service resolution (relationship graph) to evaluate.

entries.rule: Assignment groups referenced across all three processes with zero active members
entries.support_reason: The union of ITSM-018, ITSM-065 and ITSM-101 over one membership resolution, filtered to groups referenced by open records in more than one process.

entries.rule: CI owner and incident assignment group inconsistent
entries.threshold_default: Dominance threshold configurable; requires minimum incident volume per CI
entries.support_reason: Dominant assignment group per CI is a two-field group-by (cmdb_ci × assignment_group) with a minimum volume; comparing to cmdb_ci.support_group (already extracted) is an in-memory join. Dominance threshold and minimum volume UNDEFINED.
entries.volume_reason: Group-by over the incident slice; join to cmdb_ci.

entries.rule: Service referenced in incidents but absent from the CSDM model
entries.threshold_default: Includes free-text and legacy service fields where present
entries.support_reason: business_service values not present in the extracted cmdb_ci_service set — an anti-join over extracted data; "free-text and legacy service fields" are instance-specific (UNDEFINED).
entries.volume_reason: Group-by business_service plus a set lookup.
entries.implementation_notes: A reference field that dangles (sys_id with no record) vs a text value: both cases apply.

entries.rule: SLA attached to a service with no offering (commitment structurally unenforceable)
entries.support_reason: sla.js reads definitions; service_offering and cmdb_ci_service are extracted, so offering count per service is an in-memory group. Missing: parsing which services an SLA definition is scoped to (condition parsing, as ITSM-003).

entries.rule: Change conflict detection producing no results because relationships are missing
entries.threshold_default: Requires evidence that conflicts existed to be found
entries.support_reason: ITSM-084’s overlap analysis plus the relationship state between the overlapping CIs plus the incidents that followed — configuration, temporal correlation, graph and linkage in sequence.

entries.rule: Knowledge articles referenced in resolutions that are retired or unpublished
entries.support_reason: Incident→article linkage (UNDEFINED link; candidate m2m_kb_task) and kb_knowledge state — no reader for either.
